Subject: Dedicated capacity - post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from the discovery: 

- Goal: Move NexusHealth to Redwood Dedicated for production inference of clinical summarization and search reranking by Q3.
- Integration scope: SDK setup, API auth & key rotation, request routing (region-aware), structured output/tool-calling for medication extraction, and embeddings + reranker pipeline for search.
- Traffic profile (from call): ~150 rps peak for async summarization jobs, 20 qps for low-latency interactive search, average request length ~600 tokens, occasional spikes up to 8k tokens for batch exports.
- Critical non-functional: P95 latency targets for interactive search <300ms, retention/audit logs must be sent to NexusHealth SIEM.

Immediate next steps we discussed:
1) Technical integration doc & SDK quickstart (we'll share a slim guide and example repo).
2) Auth options: API keys + optional mutual TLS for private deployment.
3) Dedicated sizing + autoscaling proposal from Redwood infra team (I copied Aditya onto this thread).
4) Share SOW / integration checklist and DocuSign when ready.

I've attached a short integration checklist and draft SOW stub to speed the procurement conversation. Please confirm the traffic numbers above or flag anything missing. If the numbers look right, Aditya will follow up with concrete capacity & autoscaling guidance.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer\Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-autoscaling-sow.pdf (draft), nexus-health-integration-checklist.xlsx

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifying Qs before Aditya sizes things: 

1) For the interactive search path, can Redwood guarantee that the embeddings + reranker pipeline will keep per-query latency under 300ms at 20 qps? If not, what's the recommended design (multi-stage: fast approximate embeddings + async rerank)?

2) On SDK/auth: we currently have strict key rotation policies and prefer mutual TLS for anything in our VPC. Is that supported with Redwood Private?

3) Autoscaling: we have bursty overnight jobs at ~150 rps for bulk summarization (these are batch requests that can be queued). Will Dedicated support queue-based autoscaling, or do we need to provision for peak GPU capacity?

Also please confirm whether any of the SOW items will require data egress costs to our cloud account.

—Samir
Director, Platform Engineering\NexusHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khanna <samir.k@nexushealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Samir — great questions, answered inline below. Looping Aditya and Laura for sizing and procurement/contract items.

1) Embeddings + reranker latency:
- Short answer: Yes, we can meet the 300ms P95 for the interactive flow with the right architecture. Recommended approach: a two-stage pipeline — (a) lightweight embedding retrieval (approximate ANN using CPU-backed index + GPU-accelerated embedder) for candidate selection, then (b) GPU-based reranker for top-K (e.g., K=10). This keeps the common-path latency low; reranker runs on a small batch of candidates.
- Notes: If you need very strict SLOs for every query and can't tolerate occasional 400ms tails, we recommend reserving a small dedicated capacity pool for the reranker to avoid cold-starts.

2) SDK / Auth / Private deployment:
- SDK: We have a JS + Python quickstart that supports streaming and structured output (tool-calling hooks). We'll share the example repo (link below).
- Auth: Redwood Private supports API key + mTLS. Key rotation is supported via our control plane and we can integrate with your KMS for key material on Private.

3) Autoscaling & queues for batch summarization:
- Dedicated supports queue-based autoscaling patterns: you can push batch jobs into an internal queue (our recommended pattern) and scale a worker pool based on queue depth + processing time.
- For bursty overnight jobs we commonly recommend mixture: a baseline reserved GPU pool sized for average throughput + autoscaling workers for bursts. That avoids excessive overprovisioning while keeping tail latency bounded.

I attached a brief diagram and a sizing worksheet (see attachment). Aditya — can you propose a concrete baseline + autoscaling policy for the numbers above? E.g., baseline GPUs, expected throughput per GPU at 600 tokens avg, queue concurrency limits, and recommended max burst size.

Links:
- Integration quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart (example)
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samir Khanna <samir.k@nexushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - autoscaling & integration follow-up (sizing proposal)

Hi all — putting some concrete numbers here based on the traffic profile Marissa captured. Assumptions: 600-token average for interactive, 600-token avg for summarization (batch can spike). Using our Redwood-verified throughput profiles for the chosen reranker + embedder model: ~2000 tokens/sec per GPU for mixed workload (conservative).

Baseline sizing proposal (initial):
- Interactive search (20 qps, 600 tokens avg): ~20 * 600 = 12k tokens/sec. At 2000 t/s per GPU -> 6 GPUs to handle interactive load with headroom.
- Reranker dedicated pool: reserve 1-2 GPUs to keep P95 low (small pool avoids cold start).
- Batch summarization (150 rps peak, 600 tokens avg) -> 90k tokens/sec during peak. That would be ~45 GPUs if provisioned purely for peak. Instead we recommend: baseline reserved GPUs for the average batch throughput + autoscale workers to handle peak. Example: baseline 10 GPUs + autoscale up to 40 GPUs driven by queue depth and job concurrency.

Autoscaling policy suggestions:
- Metric: queue depth + 1-min average processing time. Scale up when queue depth exceeds 50 and projected wait time > 30s. Scale down with a 15-min cool-down once queue depth stays < 10.
- Concurrency limits: per-worker concurrency = 1 for GPU-bound reranker jobs; use multiple worker pods per GPU with GPU-sharing disabled for tight latency SLOs. For CPU pre-processing (embedding + ANN), allow higher concurrency (4-8).
- Queues: configure separate queues for interactive (low-latency) and batch (throughput). Interactive queue should have a strict SLA-based throttling policy and fallback to a smaller model or cached results when overloaded. Batch queue can accept retries and backpressure.

Auth / network notes:
- For Private deployments in your VPC, we support mTLS termination and KMS for key material. We'll provide a template for the mTLS cert rotation and KMS integration.

Next steps:
1) Marissa/Laura: confirm that baseline numbers (6 GPUs interactive, 1-2 reranker reserve, 10 baseline + up to 40 burst for batch) are OK to include in the SOW.
2) Samir: confirm whether you want Redwood to operate the Private control plane in your VPC or if you prefer to run the on-prem package (impacting support/ops pricing).
3) We'll produce an updated SOW and attach DocuSign link when ready.

Happy to jump on a quick follow-up call if you want to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Architect\Redwood Inference
